text:
laura: Posted a focused docs PR introducing 'micro-schema' patterns for tool calls + a short Node + Python SDK snippet. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1609. Main asks: check examples for parser-compat, wording on migration, and any broken links.
docs-bot: preview build succeeded :white_check_mark: https://deploy.preview/redwood/docs/pr-1609
alex: Quick pass. Two things: the examples reference `output_spec` in the JSON examples but our SDK surfaces `response.schema`. Can we consolidate the public name to `response.schema` in snippets to avoid confusion?
laura: Ah good catch  I used an internal draft name. Will update to `response.schema`.
sameer: On parser compatibility: prefer explicit union shapes for nullable elements rather than abbreviated arrays of types. Example suggestion for nullable-item arrays: ```json
{"type":"array","items":{"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"null"}]}}
```
laura: Noted. I'll swap shorthand forms for anyOf in the examples.
priya: UX/SDK note: please add a 1-line fallback showing how to consume streamed tool outputs in both Node and Python. Users often assume non-streaming only and get surprised in production. Example snippets to mirror each other would be helpful.
jon: Product: include a short decision sentence in the migration appendix: when to keep micro-schema (smaller token cost, weaker validation) vs full JSON Schema (strict contracts). That helps teams pick a path without reading everything.
laura: Will add a single decision sentence under "Choosing schema granularity."
alex: Also there's a link pointing to /docs/old-tool-calling-guide — redirect exists but it loses anchors. Better to point to /docs/tool-calling and to the examples folder directly.
laura: Good point, fixing links. Anything else before I push updates?
sameer: One more: call out that some downstream language parsers drop keys when values are empty strings vs null. Add a short migration checklist item: "run sample payloads through downstream parsers to detect key-dropping behavior."
priya: For docs infra, I suggest adding a small linter rule (docs-lint) that flags `type: ["x","null"]` and recommends `anyOf` form. I can draft a GitHub Action for this repo if team wants.
laura: Love that. Please add a note in the PR description linking to your lint prototype if you open it.
docs-bot: preview refreshed :rocket: https://deploy.preview/redwood/docs/pr-1609?v=2
alex: Also noticed examples/invocations/micro.md is referenced as micro-invoke.md in one anchor. Filename mismatch, so fix either the link or the file.
laura: Fixing filename references and switching `output_spec` -> `response.schema`. Will also add the streaming small examples and the one-line decision sentence.
sameer: Pushed a tiny wording tweak for the nullable arrays paragraph and added a note about parsers that coerce empty strings. No ML blockers.
priya: I'll open the linter prototype in a follow-up PR and reference it here.
laura: Thanks all. Planning to merge after one more CI run unless someone objects. Merge window in ~10m.
jon: :thumbsup: ship it after CI.
laura: Merging if green. Appreciate the quick feedback!
